content: I’ll first read the workspace instructions and the two applicable skills: the required fish-control bookshelf protocol and the wake-visual inspection workflow. Then I’ll inspect the inherited rollout evidence before touching the policy.

The wake-visual skill makes the keyframe sheets mandatory evidence, and the bookshelf requires mechanism-level transfer rather than gain copying. I’m now anchoring the visuals to scores, observations, metrics, inherited notes, and the current policy before forming the candidate hypothesis.

The four sampled solver examples are byte-identical—not independent behavior—and all show the same finite capture. The released sheet shows a compact self-propelled diagonal approach through developed wakes, with no visible detour or terminal overshoot; there is no sampled failure sheet to compare, so I’ll use the inherited failure records only as nonvisual counterevidence and won’t invent a visual failure diagnosis.

The shelf is now influencing the edit: I’m translating one invariant from wake-adaptive/closed-loop rhythmic control—yield a propulsive command only when sensed hydrodynamic assistance and observed targetward motion agree. The translation will be a small, phase-preserving posterior reference governor, normalized by gait state and body-frame load; no vortex phase, published gain, or route is transferred.

The candidate now makes one bounded structural change: a maximum 3% posterior-wave reference yield, activated only by the conjunction of coherent closure, target-aligned yaw assistance, and reinforcing actuator pressure. The reusable guidance has been revised with the evaluated signed-moment result and explicitly separates its faster closure from unproven load relief or wake robustness.

I’ve read the mandated checker definition. It calls for three non-CFD checks—guidance provenance, a Julia contract smoke test, and the workspace boundary audit—which I’ll run separately and repair if any fail.

The first check exposed a pre-existing workspace-rendering defect: `README.md` marks the same parent twice, so the checker refuses to choose one before it even compares my guidance. I’m inspecting the checker and marker context to determine whether this can be resolved without changing any protected task content.

The Julia smoke check is blocked by the runner environment, not the policy: `julia` is absent from `PATH` (the shell also emits unrelated missing-SSH-key setup warnings). I’ll locate any workspace/system Julia binary, then run the exact check with a non-login shell if one exists.

The checker’s Julia command now passes using the installed Julia 1.12.2 binary discovered behind the workspace wrapper; the policy contract is sound. The boundary audit also passes. I’m invoking the configured check-runner once more as required, with the binary-path workaround, while I perform a targeted activation/invariance test locally.
